mitigations.primitive_impact: The write condition depends on the ASLR-randomized stack residue byte at rbp-0xf being 0x0a. This is not attacker-controllable. The write may or may not occur depending on ASLR randomization, making it unreliable.

mitigations.name: CET (SHSTK+IBT)
mitigations.primitive_impact: No direct impact on this write primitive. CET protects control flow integrity, not data writes. The write target is stack padding, not a return address or function pointer.

evidence.description: Conditional write path: cmp al, 0x0a (compare OOB-read byte against newline); jne 0x1ce9 (skip write if not newline); mov BYTE PTR [rbp+rax*1-0xe], 0x0 (write NULL to rbp-0xf if byte was newline). The write uses the same OOB index rax=0xFFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF, targeting rbp-0xf.

gdb verification: At cmp al, 0x0a, the byte read from rbp-0xf was 0xea (not 0x0a). The jne was taken, skipping the write. In all test runs, the stack residue byte was 0xea (part of stack address 0x7fffffffea50), never 0x0a. The conditional write path exists in code but was not triggered.

Stack layout verified: write target rbp-0xf is in padding between read_return (rbp-0x14) and guess buffer (rbp-0xe). Distance to canary (rbp-0x8) = 7 bytes. Distance to return address (rbp+0x8) = 23 bytes. The write does not reach any security-critical stack data.

verification_result.details: The conditional write path was verified to exist in the code (cmp al, 0x0a; jne skip; mov byte, 0x0 at 0x1ce4). However, in all dynamic test runs, the stack residue byte at rbp-0xf was 0xea (part of ASLR-randomized stack address), not 0x0a, so the write was never triggered. The write condition (byte == 0x0a) depends on ASLR-randomized stack content that is not attacker-controllable. Even if triggered, the write target (rbp-0xf) is stack padding 7 bytes away from the canary and 23 bytes from the return address, with no security-critical data at the target offset. Marked CANDIDATE because the write path exists but was not dynamically observed to execute.

primitives.notes: PRIM-002 is a RESTRICTED_WRITE (conditional 1-byte NULL write), not ARB_WRITE or RELATIVE_WRITE. The write target is a fixed stack offset (rbp-0xf), not attacker-controllable. The write value is always 0x00 (NULL, hardcoded). The write condition depends on ASLR-randomized stack residue being 0x0a, which is not attacker-controllable. Even if the write occurs, it targets stack padding with no security-critical data. The primitive is marked CANDIDATE because: (1) the write path exists in code, (2) the condition was never met in test runs (byte was always 0xea), (3) the condition is not attacker-controllable, (4) even if triggered, the impact is minimal (zeroing a padding byte). This primitive cannot be upgraded to VERIFIED without observing the actual write, which requires the ASLR-dependent stack byte to coincidentally be 0x0a.

non_primitives.reason: The OOB read at rbp-0f reads 1 byte of stack residue, but the value is never output to the user. It is used only for an internal comparison (cmp al, 0x0a) to decide whether to strip a newline. The read byte does not appear in any program output. Therefore, no information leakage occurs. INFO_LEAK requires the leaked information to be observable in program output, which does not happen here.

The OOB read target is a fixed stack offset (rbp-0xf, always 1 byte before the guess buffer). The attacker cannot control the target address - it is always rbp-0xf regardless of input. ARB_READ requires the target address to be attacker-controllable. This is at most a RESTRICTED_READ (single fixed offset, 1 byte).

The OOB write target is a fixed stack offset (rbp-0xf). The attacker cannot control the target address. The write value is always 0x00 (NULL, hardcoded). ARB_WRITE requires both target address and write value to be attacker-controllable. This is at most a RESTRICTED_WRITE (single fixed offset, NULL-only value, conditional on stack residue).

The OOB write at rbp-0xf does not reach the stack canary (7 bytes away at rbp-0x8) or the return address (23 bytes away at rbp+0x8). The write targets only a padding byte between two local variables. There is no path to control the canary, return address, or any security-critical stack data through this primitive.

When read returns 0 and the OOB read occurs, the program does not crash. The OOB read targets a valid, readable stack address (rbp-0xf, within the current stack frame). The program enters an infinite loop printing 'Invalid input, please input 5 letter.' because strlen(guess_buf) != 5 (the buffer contains stack residue, not a valid 5-char string). The program continues looping indefinitely without crashing. No SIGSEGV or other crash signal is produced.

unresolved.description: Whether the conditional OOB write (PRIM-002) can ever be triggered in practice
unresolved.reason: The write requires the stack residue byte at rbp-0xf to be exactly 0x0a (newline). This byte is part of the ASLR-randomized stack address (specifically, the second byte of the saved rbp value stored in the padding region). Under ASLR, stack addresses are randomized, and this byte could theoretically be 0x0a, but the probability is low (~1/256) and not attacker-controllable. In all test runs, the byte was 0xea.
unresolved.required_next_step: To verify the write path, one would need to either: (1) run the program many times until ASLR produces a stack address with 0x0a as the second byte, or (2) use gdb to artificially set the byte at rbp-0xf to 0x0a before the cmp instruction and observe the write. Option (2) would confirm the write mechanism but would not prove attacker controllability.

source.root_cause: In addWordsToList, realloc(word_list, word_count*8) return value is stored directly to context.word_list (at 0x208e) without any NULL check. If realloc fails (returns NULL due to memory exhaustion), word_list becomes NULL. The subsequent write word_list[word_count-1] = strdup(token) computes destination as NULL + (word_count*8 - 8), a near-NULL address, causing SIGSEGV.
source.description: Missing NULL check on realloc return value in addWordsToList. When realloc fails, word_list is set to NULL, and the subsequent array write targets a NULL-derived address.

chain: BUG-003
Missing NULL check on realloc return in addWordsToList
realloc returns NULL (memory exhaustion) -> word_list = NULL
Write target computed as NULL + (word_count*8 - 8) = near-NULL address
mov [rbx], rax at addWordsToList+0xd7 writes strdup result to near-NULL address
NULL_POINTER_DEREF / CRASH

controlled_element.what: The write target address is NULL + (word_count*8 - 8), where word_count is influenced by the number of valid 5-char alpha tokens in the import buffer. The written value is a heap pointer (strdup result). Neither the target address nor the written value is directly attacker-controlled to arbitrary values.
controlled_element.how: Attacker controls the number of tokens in the import buffer (via importWords), which determines word_count. However, word_count starts at 5 (from setup) and the write target is always near-NULL for practical word_count values. The written value is a heap pointer from strdup, not directly attacker-controlled.

preconditions.description: realloc(word_list, word_count*8) must fail (return NULL). This requires memory exhaustion, which can be influenced by requesting very large allocations via importWords with large size values, or by importing many words to grow word_list.
preconditions.necessity: Without realloc failure, word_list remains a valid pointer and the write is in-bounds. The NULL deref only occurs when realloc returns NULL.

preconditions.description: addWordsToList must be called with a buffer containing at least one valid 5-char alpha token (to trigger the realloc+write path). This is achievable via importWords menu option 2.
preconditions.necessity: The realloc and subsequent write only execute when a valid token is found by strtok. Without a valid token, the code path is not reached.

preconditions.description: The import buffer must be properly delivered to addWordsToList. Due to scanf/read buffering interaction, the buffer contents depend on stdin buffering behavior. Using pwntools process() with direct send() ensures proper delivery.
preconditions.necessity: If the buffer is not properly delivered (e.g., scanf consumes data that read expects), addWordsToList may process uninitialized data instead of attacker-controlled tokens.

verification_plan.method: GDB-based simulation of realloc failure. Since real memory exhaustion is difficult to trigger reliably in a sandboxed environment, GDB is used to force realloc's return value to NULL (set $rax=0 after realloc returns), then observe the crash at the write instruction. This is valid because: (1) the code path is identical - only realloc's return value differs; (2) the bug is the MISSING NULL CHECK, not the realloc call; (3) GDB forcing rax=0 after realloc is equivalent to realloc returning NULL; (4) the subsequent code path (store NULL to word_list, compute write target, attempt write) executes exactly as in a real failure.
verification_plan.environment: Linux x86-64, glibc 2.39, PIE binary with Full RELRO/NX/Canary/SHSTK+IBT. GDB used to simulate realloc failure.
expected_evidence: realloc returned rax=0x55555555b6b0 (success), then forced to 0 (NULL)
word_count = 6, word_count*8-8 = 40 = 0x28
Expected write target if word_list=NULL: 0x28
SIGSEGV at addWordsToList+0xd7 (0x5555555560c3)
rbx (write target) = 0x28 (near-NULL)
rax (strdup result) = 0x55555555b6f0
fault_address = 0x28 (near-NULL, proving NULL-derived write target)

mitigations.name: Full RELRO
mitigations.primitive_impact: Not relevant. This bug is a heap/NULL pointer issue, not a GOT overwrite. Full RELRO does not prevent or mitigate this primitive.

mitigations.name: NX
mitigations.primitive_impact: Not relevant. The crash is a NULL dereference, not code execution on stack/heap.

mitigations.name: Stack Canary
mitigations.primitive_impact: Not relevant. The bug is in heap memory (word_list pointer in .bss), not stack overflow.

mitigations.name: PIE
mitigations.primitive_impact: Not relevant. The write target is NULL-derived (near-NULL address), independent of binary base address.

mitigations.name: SHSTK+IBT (CET)
mitigations.primitive_impact: Not relevant. The primitive is a NULL dereference crash, not control flow hijacking.

evidence.description: realloc(word_list, word_count*8) called at 0x2089. Return value in rax stored directly to context.word_list (0x5070) at 0x208e via 'mov QWORD PTR [rip+0x2fdb], rax' without any NULL check.

After realloc, word_list is loaded from context (0x5070). If realloc failed, this is NULL. Destination computed as rbx = word_list + (word_count*8 - 8) at 0x20a1-0x20b7. strdup result written to [rbx] at 0x20c3 via 'mov QWORD PTR [rbx], rax'. If word_list is NULL, this writes to NULL + offset.
GDB verification: realloc returned 0x55555555b6b0 (success). Forced rax=0 (NULL) to simulate realloc failure. word_count=6 at this point, so expected write target = NULL + (6*8-8) = 0x28.

GDB verification: After forcing word_list=NULL, SIGSEGV occurred at 0x5555555560c3 (addWordsToList+0xd7, 'mov [rbx], rax'). rbx=0x28 (write target = NULL + 0x28), rax=0x55555555b6f0 (strdup result). fault_address=0x28 (near-NULL, proving NULL-derived write target). Backtrace: addWordsToList <- importWords <- main.

verification_result.details: GDB forced realloc return to NULL (simulating memory exhaustion). word_list became NULL. Write target computed as NULL + (word_count*8 - 8) = NULL + 0x28 = 0x28. SIGSEGV at addWordsToList+0xd7 (mov [rbx], rax) when attempting to write strdup result (0x55555555b6f0) to address 0x28. fault_address=0x28 confirms NULL-derived write target. The primitive is a direct NULL pointer dereference causing crash. Cannot be upgraded to ARB_WRITE or RELATIVE_WRITE because: (1) write target is always near-NULL for practical word_count values (word_count starts at 5, max practical ~millions, giving target ~0x7A11F8 which is still in unmapped low-address space); (2) written value is a heap pointer from strdup, not directly attacker-controlled.

primitives.notes: The primitive is a NULL_POINTER_DEREF / CRASH. It cannot be upgraded to a write primitive (ARB_WRITE/RELATIVE_WRITE) because: (1) The write target is NULL + (word_count*8 - 8), which is always a near-NULL address for practical word_count values. word_count starts at 5 (from setup loading /etc/words.txt) and can only increase. Even with millions of imported words, the target remains in the low megabyte range, which is unmapped in standard Linux user space. (2) The written value is a heap pointer from strdup(token), which is not directly attacker-controlled (it depends on heap allocator state). (3) The trigger condition (realloc failure via memory exhaustion) is difficult to achieve in practice but the code path is unambiguously buggy - the missing NULL check is a clear defect. Verification was performed by GDB-forced NULL return, which is equivalent to real realloc failure since the subsequent code path is identical.

non_primitives.reason: Cannot upgrade to ARB_WRITE. The write target is NULL + (word_count*8 - 8), always near-NULL for practical word_count values. The target address is not attacker-controllable to arbitrary values. The written value (strdup heap pointer) is also not directly attacker-controlled.

Cannot upgrade to RELATIVE_WRITE. While the write target has a relative offset from NULL (word_count*8 - 8), the base is NULL (address 0), not a valid base address. The target is always in unmapped low-address space, so no actual write occurs - only a crash.
